title: 106th Rescue Wing aid in submarine search
description: B-Roll of U.S. Air Force National Guardsmen with the 106th Rescue Wing and HC-130 Combat King II loadmaster, Tech. Sgt. Steven Benza, June 21, 2023 at F.S Gabreski Air National Guard Base, Westhampton Beach, New York. Airmen walking  to the Aircraft are preparing to be scanners for the missing Titan submarine.  (U.S. Air Force National Guard video by Capt. Campbell)

transcript.text: Hi, I'm Steve Fenza from the Wonder 6th Rescue Wing.
Today we're pre-flighted our H2-130J aircraft to go out and do a search mission for the missing types of person.
And we're getting the airplane ready to fly.
We're checking all our systems to make sure they all work before we go out into the water.
And some of the things we use while we're searching, if we find somebody in the water, we have different rescue kits available.
This is an MA-2 rescue kit, and it's connected to five bundles connected with buoyant rope in between.
So that thick piece spots someone in the water. We can fly over that and throw out a bundle of one, two, three, four and five connected by that floating rope.
And hopefully the wind and the current will take the kit and wrap it around the survivor.
In the kits we have wraps and other survival communication equipment that we can give the person to survive longer in the water
until weeks we go and get some help. We'll pick them up.
